name: elevenlabs
summary: Successfully completed the ElevenLabs quickstart end-to-end. Installed the elevenlabs and python-dotenv packages, created example.py with the quickstart's text-to-speech code, and ran it. The script successfully generated a 43KB MP3 audio file (MPEG ADTS layer III, 128 kbps, 44.1 kHz) at /home/daytona/output.mp3 from the input text "The first move is what sets everything in motion." using the George voice (JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb) and eleven_v3 model.
deviations: The quickstart uses `play(audio)` to play audio through speakers. Since the sandbox has no audio output hardware, I substituted `save(audio, "/home/daytona/output.mp3")` to write the generated audio to a file instead. This is the only deviation; all other steps (SDK installation, API key from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY env var, voice ID, model ID, output format) followed the quickstart exactly.

verified.evidence: /home/daytona/output.mp3: Audio file with ID3 version 2.4.0, contains: MPEG ADTS, layer III, v1, 128 kbps, 44.1 kHz, Monaural

friction.detail: The script uses api_key=os.getenv("ELEVENLABS_API_KEY") but the transcript never shows an export, .env creation, or other auth step that a first-time developer would need to replicate.

The fetched quickstart returns navigation noise instead of concise steps: "ElevenAPI quickstart | ElevenLabs Documentation For AI agents: a documentation index is available at the root level at /llms.txt..."

The code hardcodes a voice_id with only a comment to browse a library, leaving developers to guess how to obtain a valid ID: "voice_id=\"JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb\",  # \"George\" - browse voices at elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library"
